items.evidence: The adjective 'durable' coordinates grammatically with the adjective 'attractive' across the conjunction 'and'.
The subject phrase 'The number of...' takes a singular verb ('is').
The subject 'Several members' is plural, requiring the plural base verb 'travel'.
Indefinite pronouns starting with 'Every' (like 'Every employee') take singular verbs ('has').
The time marker 'Last month' requires the simple past tense ('exceeded').
The presence of 'since she graduated' indicates an action starting in the past and continuing into the present, requiring the present perfect tense ('has worked').
An ongoing past action interrupted by another uses the past continuous tense ('was checking').
Specific times of the clock take the preposition 'at'.
Specific days and dates take the preposition 'on'.
To indicate an action or state continuing up to a specific time, 'until' is used.
